source_title: Iran war live: Araghchi says talks under way on 2-day plan to reopen Hormuz
source_excerpt: These were the updates on the US-Israel war on Iran from Sunday, November 1, 2026. Iran FM Araghchi calls US dialogue offer ‘a positive step’ as Iranian delegation visits Doha This live page is now closed. You can continue to follow our coverage here . This live page is now closed. You can continue to follow our coverage here . Iran warns it can inflict “devastating strikes” on US warships in the Middle East and says enemy forces attempting a ground invasion will face a “killing ground”. US President Donald Trump says negotiations with Iran are “going fine”, but he is “not in that much of a hurry” to make a peace deal. Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says talks are ongoing with Qatari mediators on a plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days if the US cooperates. Tehran’s security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, says a letter sent by US Vice President JD Vance changed the US tone “completely”, describing it as a “very positive sign”. live-orange 1h ago ( 23:59 GMT ) Our coverage continues This live page is closing. Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Bahrain and Yemen condemned the attack on Qatar’s Al Mayeda LNG carrier in the Gulf, expressing solidarity with Doha. Yemeni government forces said they had repelled a Houthi attack south of Taiz, amid renewed fighting that has disrupted food assistance to hundreds of thousands of people. Israeli forces continued their military operation in Hebron for a tenth day, raiding shops, seizing surveillance cameras and assaulting Palestinians, according to Wafa. Yemen’s foreign minister called for accountability over the death of UN employee Mohammed Ibrahim al-Shami, who had been held in Houthi custody for more than two years. Yet, agreements to stop war matter most when distrust is the deepest. The key question is whether regional governments can agree on rules that make their disagreements less destructive. In a recent lecture at Cambridge University in the UK, Oman’s Foreign Minister, Sayyid Badr Albusaidi, called for a non-aggression pact among all eight Gulf littoral states: the six members of the Gulf Cooperation Council along with Iraq and Iran. He described it as the essential prerequisite for an inclusive regional security architecture. Could such a pact work? As Albusaidi conceded, it would be hard to achieve. But as another major escalation looms between Iran and the United States, the region urgently needs a diplomatic path forward. Indeed, the ongoing conflict has proved so hard to resolve because the region’s security arrangements have remained underdeveloped, relying for too long on external powers. The way forward, then, can be an inclusive agreement. Read more here . Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi with Oman’s Foreign Minister Badr al-Busaidi in Tehran, August 25, 2026.
